events.title: David Chaum proposes cryptographic digital cash

research.summary: Chaum presented Blind Signatures for Untraceable Payments at CRYPTO '82, a direct foundation for privacy-preserving electronic cash.
research.significance: One of the clearest technical ancestors of cryptocurrency-era digital cash.

events.title: DigiCash is founded

research.summary: DigiCash was founded by David Chaum to commercialize cryptographic electronic-cash technology.
research.significance: It was the most important pre-Bitcoin commercial attempt to deploy privacy-preserving digital cash.

events.title: Cypherpunks mailing list emerges

research.summary: Eric Hughes sent the welcome message establishing the Cypherpunks mailing list infrastructure on toad.com.
research.significance: The list became a major forum for privacy, cryptography and digital-cash ideas that directly preceded Bitcoin.

events.title: A Cypherpunk's Manifesto

research.summary: Eric Hughes published A Cypherpunk's Manifesto to the Cypherpunks mailing list.
research.significance: A defining statement of the cypherpunk movement's privacy-through-code philosophy.

events.title: Adam Back creates Hashcash

research.summary: Adam Back's later Hashcash paper states that Hashcash was originally proposed in May 1997 as an anti-spam/proof-of-work mechanism.
research.significance: Bitcoin explicitly cites Hashcash-style proof of work, making this a core technical precursor.

sources.title: Hashcash — A Denial of Service Counter-Measure

events.title: Wei Dai publishes b-money

research.summary: Wei Dai published b-money in November 1998, describing protocols for money and contracts among untraceable entities.
research.significance: Satoshi cited b-money in the Bitcoin white paper; it is a direct conceptual predecessor.

events.title: Nick Szabo describes Bit Gold

research.summary: The surviving primary Bit Gold publication is Nick Szabo's 29 December 2005 post; it describes scarce digital objects created through proof of work and timestamping.
research.significance: Bit Gold is an important conceptual predecessor to Bitcoin, but the archive should not assert a 1998 publication without stronger primary evidence.
research.notes: Many secondary timelines date the concept to 1998. The verified surviving primary publication used here is 2005-12-29.

events.title: Hal Finney creates reusable proof-of-work

research.summary: Hal Finney announced RPOW, a server that exchanged Hashcash proofs for transferable reusable proof-of-work tokens.
research.significance: RPOW was a sophisticated pre-Bitcoin experiment in scarce, transferable proof-of-work-based digital value.

events.title: Bitcoin whitepaper published

research.summary: Satoshi Nakamoto posted Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System to the Cryptography Mailing List on 31 October 2008.
research.significance: This is Bitcoin's public birth as a documented protocol proposal.

sources.title: Bitcoin P2P e-cash paper — Cryptography Mailing List

events.title: Bitcoin Genesis Block

research.summary: Bitcoin's genesis block was timestamped 3 January 2009 and contains the Times bank-bailout headline in its coinbase data.
research.significance: The genesis block created the chain's starting point and one of crypto's most iconic historical artifacts.

events.title: Satoshi sends Hal Finney 10 BTC

research.summary: Block 170 contains the first known person-to-person Bitcoin transfer: 10 BTC sent by Satoshi to Hal Finney.
research.significance: The first known Bitcoin transaction between two people proved the network could transfer value.

events.title: Bitcoin Pizza Day

research.summary: Laszlo Hanyecz reported successfully trading 10,000 BTC for pizza, thanking 'jercos.'
research.significance: Bitcoin Pizza Day became the canonical story of Bitcoin crossing from digital experimentation into real-world commerce.

events.title: Bitcoin value overflow incident and emergency fix

research.summary: A value-overflow flaw was exploited in block 74,638 to create roughly 184.47 billion invalid BTC; developers rapidly patched the software and the valid chain rejected the bad history.
research.significance: Bitcoin's first catastrophic protocol bug demonstrated both early fragility and emergency coordination.

sources.title: Bitcoin v0.3.10 — overflow bug emergency fix

events.title: Silk Road launches

research.summary: US prosecutors later alleged that Ross Ulbricht created Silk Road in approximately January 2011 and operated it as an anonymous online marketplace using Bitcoin.
research.significance: Silk Road became Bitcoin's first globally notorious commercial use case and permanently linked early crypto history with censorship resistance, darknet markets and law enforcement.

sources.title: DOJ — Ross Ulbricht / Silk Road indictment

events.title: Mt. Gox becomes a dominant Bitcoin exchange

research.summary: Contemporary reporting described Mt. Gox as Bitcoin's most popular/dominant exchange during the 2011 boom.
research.significance: Mt. Gox's concentration made its failures systemically important to the young Bitcoin economy.

sources.title: WIRED — Bitcoin Prices Plummet on Hacked Exchange
WIRED — The Rise and Fall of Bitcoin

events.title: First major Mt. Gox security crisis

research.summary: A compromised Mt. Gox account was used to dump bitcoin, sending the quoted exchange price from about $17 to pennies before trading was suspended and transactions rolled back.
research.significance: The flash crash was Bitcoin's first globally visible exchange-security crisis and exposed severe operational risk at centralized exchanges.

sources.title: WIRED — Bitcoin Prices Plummet on Hacked Exchange
BitMEX Research — June 2011 Bitcoin Flash Crash

events.title: Litecoin launches

research.summary: Charlie Lee announced Litecoin on 9 October 2011; Litecoin's genesis block was mined about three days later, and the planned public launch time was 13 October.
research.significance: Litecoin became the longest-lived major early Bitcoin-derived altcoin and popularized Scrypt, faster blocks and a 'digital silver' narrative.

events.title: First Bitcoin halving

research.summary: Bitcoin's block subsidy fell from 50 BTC to 25 BTC at block 210,000 on 28 November 2012.
research.significance: The first halving proved Bitcoin's programmed monetary schedule would execute in practice and established a four-year market ritual.

events.title: HODL is born

research.summary: BitcoinTalk user GameKyuubi titled a post 'I AM HODLING,' a drunken misspelling of holding that immediately became community slang.
research.significance: HODL became one of crypto's most durable memes and a shorthand for refusing to sell through volatility.

events.title: Dogecoin launches

research.summary: Dogecoin launched on 6 December 2013, created by Billy Markus and Jackson Palmer around the Doge meme.
research.significance: Dogecoin fused cryptocurrency with internet meme culture and pioneered tipping, community fundraising and later meme-coin culture.

events.title: Ethereum whitepaper

research.summary: Ethereum's official history dates the introductory whitepaper to 27 November 2013; Vitalik Buterin had circulated the first draft to prospective collaborators that month.
research.significance: The paper proposed a general-purpose blockchain for smart contracts and decentralized applications, expanding the idea of blockchain beyond money.

events.title: Mt. Gox collapses

research.summary: Mt. Gox went offline on 25 February 2014 after halting Bitcoin withdrawals earlier in the month and filed for bankruptcy protection in Tokyo on 28 February.
research.significance: The failure of the world's former dominant Bitcoin exchange became crypto's defining early custody and counterparty disaster.

sources.title: The Guardian — MtGox collapse / withdrawal halt analysis

events.title: US government auctions seized Silk Road bitcoin

research.summary: The US Marshals Service auctioned 29,656 BTC forfeited from Silk Road infrastructure on 27 June 2014.
research.significance: A government auction of seized Bitcoin was an extraordinary early moment in which law enforcement treated BTC as a sellable asset rather than merely contraband.

sources.title: Bitcoin historical auction record — USMS June 2014

events.title: Ether crowdsale begins

research.summary: Ethereum launched its 42-day Ether genesis sale on 22 July 2014, accepting Bitcoin and initially offering 2,000 ETH per BTC.
research.significance: The crowdsale funded Ethereum's development and became a landmark precursor to the later ICO era.

sources.title: Ethereum Foundation — Launching the Ether Sale
Ethereum Foundation — Ether Sale statistical overview

events.title: Realcoin/Tether origins

research.summary: The stablecoin project began in 2014 under the Realcoin name and was renamed Tether; the first USDT tokens were issued on 6 October 2014 on the Bitcoin/Omni layer.
research.significance: Tether became the dominant crypto-native dollar instrument and one of the most consequential pieces of exchange infrastructure in crypto history.

sources.title: Tether — Eight Years of Stability and Innovation

events.title: Ethereum mainnet launches

research.summary: Ethereum's Frontier genesis launched on 30 July 2015, bringing the first live Ethereum mainnet into operation.
research.significance: This was the birth of the programmable smart-contract network that would underpin ICOs, DeFi, NFTs, DAOs and much of later crypto culture.

events.title: The DAO crowdsale

research.summary: The DAO launched a token sale on Ethereum beginning 30 April 2016 and raised more than 11.5 million ETH, then worth around $150 million.
research.significance: The DAO became an unprecedented blockchain crowdfunding and governance experiment, setting the stage for Ethereum's defining governance crisis.

sources.title: Ethereum.org — The DAO hack and Ethereum Classic

events.title: The DAO exploit

research.summary: An attacker exploited a recursive-call/reentrancy vulnerability in The DAO and began draining Ether into a child DAO.
research.significance: The exploit was the defining smart-contract security failure of early Ethereum and forced the community to confront whether code immutability should override asset recovery.

sources.title: Ethereum Foundation — Critical Update re DAO Vulnerability
Ethereum.org — The DAO hack and Ethereum Classic

events.title: DAO fork and Ethereum Classic split

research.summary: At block 1,920,000, the Ethereum hard fork moved DAO-related Ether to a refund contract; miners opposed to the intervention continued the original chain, which became Ethereum Classic.
research.significance: The split permanently demonstrated that blockchains are also governed by communities and social consensus, not code alone.

sources.title: Ethereum.org — The DAO hack and Ethereum Classic

events.title: Rare Pepes emerge on Counterparty

research.summary: The first Rare Pepe Counterparty collectible was posted in early September 2016, and the Rare Pepe Directory project was organized days later.
research.significance: Rare Pepes created a native blockchain collectible/art culture on Bitcoin before the Ethereum NFT boom.

sources.title: Book of Kek — Rare Pepe Series 1
Book of Kek — Rare Pepe Blockchain Project

events.title: CryptoPunks launches

research.summary: Larva Labs launched CryptoPunks in June 2017 as 10,000 algorithmically generated characters on Ethereum, initially claimable for free.
research.significance: CryptoPunks became the prototype for the modern profile-picture NFT collection and one of the most influential digital-ownership experiments in crypto.

events.title: ICO mania

research.summary: Token sales/ICOs expanded dramatically in 2017, with projects raising billions of dollars, largely using Ethereum and ERC-20 tokens.
research.significance: The ICO boom was crypto's first major programmable-capital-formation mania and directly prompted new securities-law enforcement.
research.notes: Era/trend row rather than one exact date; keep for book/timeline context, not necessarily a standalone card.

events.title: Binance launches

research.summary: Binance launched its exchange on 14 July 2017 after a June-to-July BNB token sale.
research.significance: Binance grew with extraordinary speed into the world's largest crypto exchange and became one of the industry's most powerful institutions.

events.title: Bitcoin Cash fork

research.summary: Bitcoin Cash split from Bitcoin after the last common Bitcoin block, height 478,558, on 1 August 2017; BCH then followed rules allowing larger blocks.
research.significance: The hard fork was the most consequential permanent split of the Bitcoin block-size war and created a rival chain with shared pre-fork history.

sources.title: IRS — Bitcoin / Bitcoin Cash hard fork background

events.title: China bans ICO fundraising

research.summary: Chinese financial regulators declared token fundraising/ICOs an unauthorized and illegal public-financing activity and ordered existing offerings to unwind.
research.significance: The ban abruptly ended China's domestic ICO boom and became one of the year's biggest regulatory shocks.

sources.title: Chinese regulators — Notice on preventing ICO financing risks

events.title: CryptoKitties mania

research.summary: Axiom Zen launched CryptoKitties publicly on 28 November 2017.
research.significance: The game's viral breeding/trading mechanics introduced NFTs to a much wider audience and visibly stressed Ethereum's transaction capacity.

events.title: BitcoinMarket.com launches

research.significance: It helped move Bitcoin price discovery from formula-based valuation toward actual exchange trading.

events.title: Gavin Andresen launches the Bitcoin Faucet

research.summary: Gavin Andresen launched a faucet that gave each visitor 5 BTC, initially funding it with 1,100 BTC.
research.significance: It lowered the barrier to experimenting with Bitcoin before easy retail on-ramps existed.

events.title: Slush Pool begins pooled Bitcoin mining

research.summary: Marek 'Slush' Palatinus announced a cooperative mining pool, widely recognized as the first public Bitcoin mining pool.
research.significance: Pooled mining changed miner economics by trading rare solo jackpots for steadier proportional payouts.

events.title: GPU mining changes Bitcoin mining

research.summary: Public GPU-mining software demonstrated large performance gains over CPU mining and began changing Bitcoin's mining economics.
research.significance: Marks a major transition in mining specialization.

sources.title: Generating Bitcoins with your video card (OpenCL/CUDA)

events.title: Satoshi Nakamoto's public involvement winds down

research.summary: Satoshi's public involvement tapered off from late 2010, with final known private correspondence in April 2011.
research.significance: The founder's disappearance is historically central, but it is a period rather than a single December 2010 event.

sources.title: Satoshi — WikiLeaks has kicked the hornet's nest
Satoshi final email to Mike Hearn

research.notes: Keep as a period/context row; specific 2011 final-message event is separate.

events.title: WikiLeaks begins accepting Bitcoin donations

research.summary: WikiLeaks publicly announced that it was accepting anonymous Bitcoin donations after conventional payment channels had been restricted.
research.significance: The episode became one of the clearest early demonstrations of Bitcoin's censorship-resistant payment narrative.

sources.title: Forbes — WikiLeaks Asks for Anonymous Bitcoin Donations
WIRED — The Rise and Fall of Bitcoin

events.title: Namecoin launches

research.summary: Namecoin was released on 18 April 2011 as an early Bitcoin-derived blockchain focused on decentralized naming.
research.significance: It was one of the first important altcoins and an early demonstration that blockchain could secure more than monetary balances.

events.title: Casascius physical bitcoins appear

research.summary: Mike Caldwell began producing Casascius physical bitcoins: funded Bitcoin private keys embedded beneath tamper-evident holograms on physical coins.
research.significance: Casascius turned an intangible digital asset into a physical bearer collectible and became an icon of early Bitcoin culture.

events.title: Bitcoin Foundation is established

research.summary: Gavin Andresen publicly announced the launch of the Bitcoin Foundation on 27 September 2012.
research.significance: It was an early attempt to standardize, protect and promote Bitcoin through an organized nonprofit body.

events.title: Coinbase begins operations

research.summary: Coinbase states that it was founded in June 2012.
research.significance: Coinbase became one of the most consequential regulated fiat on-ramps and later the first major US crypto exchange to list publicly.

events.title: Ripple/XRP Ledger era begins

research.summary: The XRP Ledger first launched in June 2012 after development by David Schwartz, Jed McCaleb and Arthur Britto.
research.significance: XRPL was an early major alternative to proof-of-work cryptocurrencies and focused on fast payments and settlement.

events.title: Cyprus banking crisis draws attention to Bitcoin

research.summary: Bitcoin rose sharply during the Cyprus banking crisis, while contemporary reporting linked part of the interest to concern over deposit losses and capital controls.
research.significance: The episode helped establish Bitcoin's 'outside the banking system' and safe-haven narrative, but the crisis should not be treated as the sole proven cause of the rally.

sources.title: CNN Money — Bitcoin prices surge post-Cyprus bailout

research.notes: Causal wording kept cautious: contemporary correlation/narrative, not proof that Cypriot depositors drove the move.

events.title: Bitcoin first trades above $100

research.summary: Bitcoin traded above $100 for the first time on 1 April 2013 on Mt. Gox-era markets.
research.significance: Crossing three figures marked Bitcoin's transition from niche experiment to an asset attracting broad speculative attention.

events.title: Silk Road is shut down and Ross Ulbricht arrested

research.summary: Federal agents arrested Ross Ulbricht in a San Francisco library and seized his laptop; the Silk Road site was shut down in the same enforcement operation.
research.significance: The takedown was a landmark test of Bitcoin-linked law enforcement, darknet-market investigation and blockchain evidence.

sources.title: FBI — Ross Ulbricht laptop / Silk Road history

events.title: Bitcoin first trades above $1,000

research.summary: Bitcoin traded above $1,000 for the first time on Mt. Gox on 27 November 2013.
research.significance: The milestone capped Bitcoin's first truly global speculative boom and made a four-digit BTC price a mainstream financial story.

events.title: China begins major restrictions on Bitcoin financial services

research.summary: Chinese authorities stated that Bitcoin was a virtual commodity rather than legal currency and barred financial and payment institutions from Bitcoin-related business.
research.significance: This was the first major national-level regulatory shock from China and began a recurring China-policy theme in crypto markets.

sources.title: People's Daily / PBOC — Bitcoin notice Q&A

events.title: Ethereum is publicly unveiled

research.summary: Ethereum was publicly introduced in January 2014, with Vitalik Buterin publishing the 'Ethereum: Now Going Public' post and presenting the project at the North American Bitcoin Conference in Miami.
research.significance: The public unveiling turned Ethereum from a circulated proposal into an organized project seeking developers, funding and users.

sources.title: Ethereum Foundation — Ethereum: Now Going Public

events.title: Ethereum Yellow Paper formalizes the protocol

research.summary: Ethereum's official timeline dates Gavin Wood's Yellow Paper to 1 April 2014.
research.significance: The Yellow Paper gave Ethereum a formal technical specification and defined the Ethereum Virtual Machine.

events.title: Counterparty expands token experimentation on Bitcoin

research.summary: Counterparty was publicly launched on 2 January 2014, with XCP distributed through a proof-of-burn mechanism on Bitcoin.
research.significance: Counterparty showed that tokens, assets and later collectibles could be built on Bitcoin years before the modern NFT boom.

events.title: Newsweek claims to identify Satoshi Nakamoto

research.summary: Newsweek published a cover story identifying Dorian Prentice Satoshi Nakamoto as Bitcoin's creator. Dorian denied involvement, and the claim was not substantiated.
research.significance: The media frenzy became one of the most famous failed attempts to unmask Satoshi and highlighted the privacy stakes around Bitcoin's creator.

sources.title: The Guardian — Dorian Nakamoto denies Bitcoin involvement

research.notes: Record explicitly as a disputed/failed identification, never as fact that Dorian was Satoshi.

events.title: Microsoft begins accepting Bitcoin for some digital purchases

research.summary: Microsoft began allowing US customers to add Bitcoin-funded credit for purchases in the Windows and Xbox stores.
research.significance: A global technology company accepting Bitcoin represented a major merchant-adoption milestone.

sources.title: Ars Technica — Microsoft accepts Bitcoin for Xbox/Windows credit

events.title: Lightning Network paper proposes Bitcoin payment channels

research.summary: Joseph Poon and Thaddeus Dryja's Lightning Network paper proposed scalable off-chain instant Bitcoin payments routed through networks of payment channels.
research.significance: Lightning became Bitcoin's dominant second-layer payments architecture and a key answer in the block-size/scaling debate.

events.title: MakerDAO project begins

research.summary: MakerDAO traces its founding to late 2014, with active development of code, architecture and documentation underway from 2015; Rune Christensen described the eDollar precursor in March 2015.
research.significance: Maker became one of Ethereum's foundational DeFi projects and ultimately created Dai, a decentralized stablecoin.
research.notes: Raw 2015 label captures active development, but founding is better dated to late 2014.

events.title: Bitstamp suffers a major hot-wallet breach

research.summary: Bitstamp said operational wallets were compromised on 4 January 2015, resulting in the loss of less than 19,000 BTC; services were temporarily suspended and later rebuilt.
research.significance: It was a major post-Mt.Gox exchange-security test and reinforced the importance of cold storage and operational compartmentalization.

events.title: Second Bitcoin halving

research.summary: Bitcoin's second halving reduced the block subsidy from 25 BTC to 12.5 BTC on 9 July 2016.
research.significance: It reinforced Bitcoin's fixed issuance schedule and established halvings as recurring global market and mining events.

events.title: Bitfinex hack

research.summary: Bitfinex suffered a security breach on 2 August 2016 in which 119,755 BTC were stolen.
research.significance: It was one of crypto's largest exchange thefts and later became remarkable for both BFX loss tokens and a massive law-enforcement recovery.

events.title: Zcash launches

research.summary: Zcash launched its Sprout mainnet on 28 October 2016 with zk-SNARK-based shielded transactions.
research.significance: Zcash brought production zero-knowledge privacy to a permissionless cryptocurrency and made advanced cryptography a mainstream crypto topic.

sources.title: Electric Coin Company — Zcash Launch and Roadmap

events.title: ERC-20 token standard drives token issuance

research.summary: Although EIP-20 was created in November 2015, ERC-20 became the dominant fungible-token interface during the 2017 token-sale boom.
research.significance: Standardized token behavior made it easy for wallets, exchanges and ICOs to interoperate, enabling the explosive growth of Ethereum tokens.
research.notes: Do not date ERC-20's creation to 2017; 2017 is its mass-adoption/ICO era.

events.title: SegWit activates on Bitcoin

research.summary: Segregated Witness activated on Bitcoin mainnet in August 2017 after locking in earlier that month.
research.significance: SegWit fixed transaction malleability, increased effective block capacity and enabled more robust payment-channel systems such as Lightning.

events.title: Bitcoin block-size war reaches its climax

research.summary: Bitcoin's years-long block-size conflict reached its decisive phase in 2017 through SegWit, UASF pressure, the New York Agreement, the Bitcoin Cash fork and SegWit2x cancellation.
research.significance: The dispute defined Bitcoin's governance culture and clarified that miners, businesses, developers and users each had limited but meaningful power.

sources.title: Digital Currency Group — Bitcoin Scaling Agreement at Consensus 2017
IRS — Bitcoin / Bitcoin Cash hard fork background

events.title: Japan introduces a registration regime for crypto exchanges

research.summary: Japan's revised payment-services regime took effect on 1 April 2017, requiring virtual-currency exchange service providers to register.
research.significance: Japan became one of the first major economies to establish a formal registration regime for crypto exchanges.

sources.title: Japan FSA — crypto exchange registration system

events.title: CME Bitcoin futures launch

research.summary: CME listed its Bitcoin futures contract on 17 December for the 18 December trade date.
research.significance: CME brought Bitcoin into one of the world's largest regulated derivatives markets and established a major institutional price-discovery venue.

sources.title: CME — initial listing of Bitcoin futures

events.title: Bitcoin approaches $20,000 in the first global crypto mania

research.summary: Bitcoin reached its 2017 cycle peak near $20,000 in mid-December, with exact all-time-high figures varying by exchange and index.
research.significance: The peak capped the first global retail crypto mania and preceded the 2018 crypto winter.

sources.title: CoinDesk — Bitcoin Price Index historical 2017 high

events.title: Parity multisig exploit drains wallets

research.summary: A vulnerability in Parity's multisig wallet library was exploited to steal roughly 153,000 ETH from several high-profile wallets.
research.significance: The attack was one of Ethereum's largest early smart-contract wallet failures and reinforced the importance of shared-library security.

research.significance: The incident became a legendary example of smart-contract composability risk: one library failure immobilized many independent treasuries.
